title: NV_IMAGE_BLIT (0x9F) SRCCOPY guest-VRAM oracle (v0.4 — adds host-visible oracle channel via IO port 0xE9; 8-cell sweep + per-cell first-mismatch diag preserved from v0.3)
purpose: Tier-2 NV2A diag XBE covering §H.6 (`NV_IMAGE_BLIT` class 0x9F + `NV_CONTEXT_SURFACES_2D` class 0x62) per `nv2a-feature-surface-research.md`. 4x2 dashboard grid (160x240 cells); each cell encodes one IMAGE_BLIT verdict from a CPU-side oracle that compared destination VRAM byte-by-byte against the expected blit result. Single LE_A8R8G8B8 color format, SRCCOPY operation only. Source surface is a CPU-painted 32x32 buffer with four 16x16 quadrants (RED/GREEN/BLUE/WHITE); each destination surface is 64x64 sentinel-gray (0xFF808080), large enough to detect any over-write past the declared rect. The 8 cells sweep (in_x/in_y, out_x/out_y, width, height) across baseline / size / src-offset / dst-offset / both-offsets / degenerate-width / degenerate-height combinations. After each blit the XBE calls pb_wait_until_gr_not_busy(), reads dst VRAM via pb_agp_access() (cache-coherent linear remap), and verifies every pixel inside the declared dst rect equals the corresponding src pixel and every pixel outside the rect remains sentinel. Per-cell verdict is rendered as a 160x240 dashboard cell: PASS is solid green (0xFF00FF00); FAIL (v0.3) is a 2x2 sub-rect (TL=solid red FAIL banner, TR=GOT pixel color, BL=EXPECTED pixel color, BR=encoded first-mismatch (mx,my) with R/G bucket-of-32 and B nibble-packed upper 3 bits). The host harness's strict byte-exact compare against the math-derived oracle (8 all-green cells) fails immediately if any single blit misbehaves. M15 default-on second-wave Gate 2 coverage per `metal-renderer-plan.md` + `renderer-metal.md`. Catalog reference: §H.6 in nv2a-feature-surface-research.md (`NV09F_SET_OBJECT/SET_CONTEXT_SURFACES/SET_OPERATION/CONTROL_POINT_IN/CONTROL_POINT_OUT/SIZE` + `NV062_SET_OBJECT/SET_CONTEXT_DMA_IMAGE_SOURCE/SET_CONTEXT_DMA_IMAGE_DESTIN/SET_COLOR_FORMAT/SET_PITCH/SET_OFFSET_SOURCE/SET_OFFSET_DESTIN`). pbkit pre-bind makes this XBE self-contained: SUBCH_3=ChannelID 16 (0x9F), SUBCH_4=ChannelID 17 (0x62). v0.2: routes IMAGE_SOURCE / IMAGE_DESTIN through pbkit handles 3/4 (base=0, Limit=MAXRAM, untouched by `set_draw_buffer()`) — NOT 9/11, which `pb_init->pb_target_back_buffer()->set_draw_buffer()` reprograms to point at the back buffer with `limit=height*pitch-1` (`lib/pbkit/pbkit.c:1611-1668,3260`). Verified via `-trace events=nv2a_dma_map`. v0.2 status: bounded partial on Metal — 3 of 8 cells PASS byte-correct (0, 4, 5; all `width==height==8` with `(in_x,in_y) ≤ (4,4)`); 5 fail (1, 2, 3, 6, 7). Residual hypothesis points at shared blit copy/clip math (`mtl/blit.c:181-233`) or `nv_clip_gpu_tile_blit` against UnleashX-inherited PFB tile registers. See README §Status for full per-cell verdict + next-session investigation list.
expected_fail_notes: v0.4 bounded slice 2026-05-22 cycle 15: per-cell PASS/FAIL verdicts are now ALSO mirrored to xemu stderr via the `xemu-guest-log:` IO-port sink (XEMU_GUEST_LOG=1 enables it on the host; XBE writes one-byte-at-a-time to fixed port 0xE9 via `xbed_host_log_writef`). Inert on real Xbox and on stock xemu without the device wired in. Verdict semantics unchanged from v0.3 (same 3/8 PASS first-run on Metal). Cycle 15 added GL to `expected_fail_renderers` because the new host-log evidence shows GL produces the IDENTICAL `pass=3/8 mask=0x31` (cells 0, 4, 5 PASS) on the first run, confirming the cycle-13 PFIFO/PGRAPH race hypothesis is renderer-agnostic (the §H.6 residual lives in shared PFIFO/PGRAPH machinery upstream of either renderer, NOT in the renderer itself). Mask drift across reboots within a single 35s harness window (subsequent runs sometimes show 0x30 / cell 0 FAIL) is expected per the race-window hypothesis — small race window, small per-boot variance. Harness anchor lines: `image-blit: begin v0.4 host-log channel ...`, `image-blit: cell N PASS|FAIL`, optional `image-blit: cell N mismatch ...`, terminal `image-blit: tally pass=N/8 mask=0xXX`. First-run host-log evidence captured 2026-05-22 12:31 CDT under `benchmark-runs/xbe-cycle15-host-log-20260522-123038/{metal,gl}/xemu.log`. Both legs will continue to FAIL the pixel oracle (and the GL leg additionally hits the upstream GL display-capture gap) until cycle-13 follow-up #2 (`XEMU_DIAG_PGRAPH_STATUS_DRAIN`) lands. v0.3 bounded partial 2026-05-22 cycle 12: same 3/8 PASS verdict as v0.2 (cells 0, 4, 5), 5/8 FAIL (cells 1, 2, 3, 6, 7). Cycle 12 added per-cell first-mismatch diagnostic encoding (2x2 sub-rect layout per FAIL cell carrying TL=red banner / TR=got pixel / BL=expected pixel / BR=encoded (mx,my)). Decoded result: every FAIL cell shows got=0xff808080 (sentinel), expected=0xffff0000 (RED), first mismatch at (mx=0, my=0). A transient xemu-side fprintf (since reverted) proved that the renderer's CPU memcpy writes the correct RED bytes at the right host pointer for ALL 8 cells. A cached-read control experiment (oracle reading via s_dst_vram[idx] directly) made the result strictly WORSE (only cell 4 PASS). Conclusion: residual 5-cell mismatch is a guest CPU cache-coherency issue on the VRAM read-back path, NOT a renderer bug. Cycle-11 hypotheses (shared blit math, tile clipping, surface-cache download) are DISPROVED. Cycle-13 audit reframed it to a PFIFO ↔ vCPU dispatch race against missing NV_PGRAPH_STATUS publication. Cycle-15 host-log evidence now CONFIRMS the reframed race hypothesis end-to-end via GL/Metal parity. See README.md §Status + decision-log cycle 12/13/15 entries.
